358739.title: The shrunken Weyl chamber conjecture for affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties
358739.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be the reductive group in the setup, let $x=w\varepsilon^\mu\in\widetilde W$ lie in a shrunken Weyl chamber, so that $\operatorname{LP}(x)=\{v\}$ for a uniquely determined $v\in W$, and let $[b]\in B(G)$. If $X_x(b)\neq\emptyset$, define $D\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}$ by

$$
\dim X_x(b)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\ell(x)+D-\langle\nu(b),2\rho\rangle-\operatorname{defect}(b)\right),
$$

and let $C\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 1}$ be the number of $J_b(F)$-orbits of top-dimensional irreducible components of $X_x(b)$. Write $\lambda(b)$ for the relevant Kottwitz invariant and define either of the multisets

$$
E_1=\{e\mid(\omega,e)\in\operatorname{wts}(v\Rightarrow\sigma(wv)),\ \lambda(b)\equiv v^{-1}\mu-\omega\in X_\ast(T)_\Gamma\}_m,
$$

$$
E_2=\{e\mid(\omega,e)\in\operatorname{wts}(v\Rightarrow\sigma(wv)),\ \nu(b)=\operatorname{conv}(v^{-1}\mu-\omega)\}_m.
$$

Let $E$ be either $E_1$ or $E_2$. **The shrunken Weyl chamber conjecture.** The predictions are: (a) $X_x(b)\neq\emptyset$ if and only if $E\neq\emptyset$ and $\kappa(x)=\kappa(b)\in\pi_1(G)_\Gamma$; for $E=E_1$, the Kottwitz condition is automatic. (b) If $X_x(b)\neq\emptyset$, then $\max(E)=D$. (c) If $X_x(b)\neq\emptyset$, then $C$ is at most the multiplicity of $D$ in $E$, which may be $+\infty$ for $E_2$.

358888.title: Ikeda–Kitabeppu–Takai–Uehara's curvature formula conjecture
358888.literal_statement:
Let $H=(V,E)$ be the hypergraph under consideration, with vertex distance $d$, hypergraph Laplacian $
\mathcal{L}$, canonical restriction $\mathcal{L}^0$, IKTU curvature $\kappa_{\mathrm{IKTU}}(x,y)$, and weak Lipschitz class $\mathsf{Lip}_w^1(V)$. For vertices $x,y$, define

$$
\mathsf{Lip}_w^1(V;x,y)=\left\{f\in\mathsf{Lip}_w^1(V)\mid \langle f,\delta_x-\delta_y\rangle=d(x,y)\right\}
$$

and

$$
\mathcal{C}(x,y)=\frac{1}{d(x,y)}\inf_{f\in\mathsf{Lip}_w^1(V;x,y)}\langle\mathcal{L}^0f,\delta_x-\delta_y\rangle.
$$

**Ikeda–Kitabeppu–Takai–Uehara's conjecture.** For any $x,y\in V$,

$$
\kappa_{\mathrm{IKTU}}(x,y)=\mathcal{C}(x,y).
$$

The conjecture proposes the hypergraph analogue of the representation of LLY curvature by the graph Laplacian. One inequality is established in the paper, while the reverse inequality is stated to be open; hence the formula remains unresolved.

358893.title: Spectral projector kernel bounds on narrow windows for the two-dimensional torus
358893.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb{T}^2=\mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$, let $\lambda>2$ and $\delta<1$, and define

$$
\mathcal{A}_{\lambda,\delta}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2: \lambda-\delta<|x|<\lambda+\delta\}.
$$

Let

$$
\Phi_{\lambda,\delta}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal{A}_{\lambda,\delta}\cap\mathbb{Z}^2}e^{2\pi i k\cdot x},
$$

so that $P_{\lambda,\delta}f=\Phi_{\lambda,\delta}*f$. **Kernel conjecture.** If $p\geq2$ and $\kappa>0$, then, whenever $\delta>\lambda^{-1+\kappa}$,

$$
\|\Phi_{\lambda,\delta}\|_{L^p}\lesssim_{p,\kappa}\lambda^{1-\frac2p}\delta+(\lambda\delta)^{\frac12}.
$$

Equivalently, the bound is governed by $(\lambda\delta)^{1/2}$ for $2\leq p\leq4$, by that term for $p\geq4$ and $\delta<\lambda^{4/p-1}$, and by $\lambda^{1-2/p}\delta$ for $p\geq4$ and $\delta>\lambda^{4/p-1}$. The conjecture is partially equivalent to the spectral projector conjecture and is connected to additive energies of lattice points in thin annuli.

359059.title: Ceballos–Pons realization conjecture for the $s$-permutahedron
359059.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{s}$ be a weak composition. The **$\operatorname{s}$-permutahedron** $\text{Perm}_{\operatorname{s}}$ is the polyhedral subdivision associated with the $\operatorname{s}$-weak order.

**Ceballos–Pons realization conjecture.** The $\operatorname{s}$-permutahedron $\text{Perm}_{\operatorname{s}}$ can be realized as a polyhedral subdivision of a polytope that is combinatorially isomorphic to the zonotope

$$
\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq n}s_j[\mathbf e_i,\mathbf e_j],
$$

where $(\mathbf e_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ is the canonical basis of $\mathbb R^n$, and $[\mathbf e_i,\mathbf e_j]$ is the convex hull of $\mathbf e_i$ and $\mathbf e_j$.

This conjecture seeks a geometric realization of the $\operatorname{s}$-weak order, whose lattice structure was proved by Ceballos and Pons. The source does not provide evidence of a resolution.

359240.title: Geometric Borovik–Cherlin conjecture for differential fields
359240.literal_statement: Let $\Delta=\{\delta_1,\dots,\delta_m\}$ be a set of $m$ commuting derivations in characteristic zero, and let $G$ be a strongly connected differential-algebraic group of $\Delta$-type $\ell$. Suppose that $G$ acts faithfully and transitively on a differential-algebraic variety $S$ of typical $\Delta$-dimension $d>0$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the constant field of some $m-\ell$ linearly independent derivations in $\operatorname{span}_{\mathcal{C}}(\Delta)$. **Geometric Borovik–Cherlin conjecture.** If $G$ acts Kolchin-generically $(d+2)$-transitively on $S$, then $(G,S)$ is isomorphic to the natural action of $\mathrm{PSL}_{d+1}(\mathcal{F})$ on $\mathbb{P}^d(\mathcal{F})$. This extends the finite-dimensional geometric formulation by replacing dimension with typical $\Delta$-dimension and allowing several commuting derivations; the source presents it as an expectation without a resolution.

359473.title: The UGVL characterization conjecture for totally bounded ultrametric spaces
359473.literal_statement:
Let $(X,d)$ be a nonempty totally bounded ultrametric space. A point $x\in X$ is **isolated** if it has a neighborhood containing no point of $X$ other than $x$. Let $\mathbf{B}_{X,d}$ be the set of open balls of $(X,d)$, let $\mathbf{Cs}_{X,d}$ be the set of centered spheres, and let $\mathbf{UGVL}$ denote the class of ultrametric spaces generated by nonnegative vertex labelings of trees. Assume that every point of $X$ is isolated.

**UGVL characterization conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. $(X,d)\in\mathbf{UGVL}$.
2. $\mathbf{B}_{X,d}\subseteq\mathbf{Cs}_{X,d}$.

This characterizes, for nonempty totally bounded ultrametric spaces with isolated points, when the space is generated by a labeled tree in terms of its open balls being centered spheres. E. Petrov proved the conjecture for finite ultrametric spaces using a different terminology and the technique of representing trees due to Gurvich and Vyalyi.

360057.title: Parameter-family conjecture for polycyclic geometric $(7m_4)$ configurations
360057.literal_statement:
Let $m>3$, and consider the voltage group $\mathbb Z_m$. For parameters $a,b$, define the two parameter sets $F_1(m;a,b)$ and $F_2(m;a,b)$ by

$$
F_1(m;a,b)=\{a,c,d,e,f,g,q,a',c',d',e',f',g',q',t\}=\{a,-a,a,b,b,-a,-2a,a,-a,a,b,b,-a,-2a,0\}
$$

for $a\geq b$ and $1\leq a,b\leq m/2$, and

$$
F_2(m;a,b)=\{a,c,d,e,f,g,q,a',c',d',e',f',g',q',t\}=\{a,b,b,b,b,b,b,a,b,b,b,b,b,b,0\}

for $a\geq b$ and $a\neq m/2$. **Parameter-family conjecture.** These parameter values lead to geometric $(7m_4)$ configurations realizable polycyclically over $\mathbb Z_m$, and there are other valid as-yet-unidentified parameter families as well. The claim is based on preliminary experiments and the source explicitly notes that further constraints on $a$ and $b$ may not yet have been identified; proving and understanding the resulting families is left for future research.

360087.title: Young-subgroup positivity conjecture for Boolean matroid Chow rings
360087.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a Boolean matroid of rank $n$, let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ act on its Chow ring, and let $\mathrm{FY}^i$ denote the associated $\mathfrak{S}_n$-set. For $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_\ell)$, write

$$
\mathfrak{S}_\lambda:=\mathfrak{S}_{\lambda_1}\times\mathfrak{S}_{\lambda_2}\times\cdots\times\mathfrak{S}_{\lambda_\ell}.
$$

**Young-subgroup positivity conjecture.** For $i\leq j\leq k\leq\ell$ with $i+\ell=j+k$, the element

$$
[\mathrm{FY}^j][\mathrm{FY}^k]-[\mathrm{FY}^i][\mathrm{FY}^\ell]\geq_{B(\mathfrak{S}_n)}0
$$

is a genuine permutation representation whose orbit stabilizers are all Young subgroups $\mathfrak{S}_\lambda$. This refines Burnside log-concavity for Boolean matroids by specifying the stabilizers occurring in the resulting permutation representation. It is presented as a conjectural strengthening suggested by the Boolean examples, while Burnside $PF_3$ itself is known to fail even in rank $4$.

376191.title: O'Neill's supersaturation conjecture for eventown families
376191.literal_statement:
Let $n>1$, let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and let $2^{[n]}$ denote the family of all subsets of $[n]$. For a family $\mathcal{A}\subset 2^{[n]}$, write $op(\mathcal{A})$ for the number of pairs of distinct members $A,B\in\mathcal{A}$ such that $|A\cap B|$ is odd. Fix an integer $s$ satisfying

$$
1\le s\le 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}-2^{\lfloor n/4\rfloor}.
$$

**O'Neill's supersaturation conjecture.** If $\mathcal{A}\subset 2^{[n]}$ consists of even-sized subsets and

$$
|\mathcal{A}|\ge 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}+s,
$$

then

$$
op(\mathcal{A})\ge s\cdot 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1}.
$$

This conjecture gives a supersaturation bound for eventown: once an even-set family exceeds the extremal size $2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, it predicts a linear lower bound on the number of pairs whose intersection has odd size. The source attributes the conjecture to O'Neill; the supplied material does not establish whether it has been resolved.

382181.title: Conjecture on totally chain-intersecting families for p at least q
382181.literal_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and let $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be a family. For positive integers $p$ and $q$, call $\mathcal F$ **totally $(p,q)$-chain intersecting** if it contains no chains $A_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq A_p$ and $B_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq B_q$ with $A_1\cap B_1=\emptyset$. For $1\leq i\leq n$, define

$$
\mathcal F_q(i)=\{F\subseteq 2^{[n]}:1\in F,\ |F|\leq i\}\cup\{F\subseteq 2^{[n]}:i-q+1\leq |F|\leq i\}.
$$

Let $\mathcal R$ denote the middle $p-1$ levels.

**Conjecture for totally chain-intersecting families.** If $\mathcal F$ is a totally $(p,q)$-chain intersecting family and $p\geq q$, then

$$
|\mathcal F|\leq\max\{ |\mathcal F_q(i)|,|\mathcal R|\}.
$$

The source explains that $\mathcal F_q(i)$ is totally $(p,q)$-chain intersecting when $p\geq q$, providing the proposed extremal construction. No resolution of this conjecture is stated in the supplied text.

382191.title: Generalized exponential polynomial conjecture for mixed additive-function equations
382191.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $\mathbb{F}\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a field, and let $p_{1},\ldots,p_{n},q_{1},\ldots,q_{n}$ be fixed positive integers satisfying conditions C(i)--C(iii). Let $f_{1},\ldots,f_{n},g_{1},\ldots,g_{n}\colon\mathbb{F}\to\mathbb{C}$ be additive functions satisfying the mixed equation from the paper. A function is a **generalized exponential polynomial function of degree at most $n-1$** if it has the corresponding finite exponential-polynomial representation of that degree. **Generalized exponential polynomial conjecture.** Every function $f_i$ and $g_i$ is a generalized exponential polynomial function of degree at most $n-1$. In particular, if

$$
f_i(x)=D_i(x),\qquad g_i(x)=\widetilde{D}_i(x)\qquad (x\in\mathbb{F}^{\times}),
$$

for derivations $D_i$ and $\widetilde{D}_i$, then the orders of $D_i$ and $\widetilde{D}_i$ are at most $n-1$. This conjecture would describe the full solution class of the mixed additive-function equation and would, in particular, bound the orders of derivations occurring among its solutions.

382198.title: Alternating subword complex equivalence conjecture
382198.literal_statement: Let $Q$ be a word in the simple generators of a finite Coxeter group, let $\omega$ be a Coxeter-group element, and let $[e,\omega]$ be the corresponding interval in the weak order. Suppose that $Q$ is **alternating**, meaning that every pair of non-commuting generators $s,t$ alternates within $Q$. The subword complex equivalence relation $\equiv_{Q,\omega}$ on $[e,\omega]$ is defined by restricting the partition into sets of linear extensions to this interval. **Alternating subword complex equivalence conjecture.** If $Q$ is alternating, then $\equiv_{Q,\omega}$ is a lattice congruence of the interval $[e,\omega]$ of the weak order. This would identify the equivalence induced by alternating subword complexes with a lattice-theoretic quotient of the weak-order interval. The supplied text does not indicate whether the assertion has been proved or remains open.

374237.title: Mixed cyclic Ramsey conjecture for alternating and monotone paths
374237.literal_statement:
Let $P_a^\mathrm{alt}$ be an alternating path of order $a$ and $P_b^\mathrm{mon}$ a monotone path of order $b$. **Mixed path conjecture.** For any $a \ge 3$ and $b \ge 4$, we have

$$
R_\mathrm{cyc}(P_a^\mathrm{alt}, P_b^\mathrm{mon}) = 1 + (a - 1)(b - 2).
$$

The claim is motivated by the computed mixed cyclic Ramsey numbers and by the discussion that the case $b=3$ is rotationally equivalent to the alternating-path case. The asserted formula remains open.

372010.title: Fox–Himwich–Zhou TAS-tree conjecture
372010.literal_statement:
An **undirected tree** is a connected graph with no cycles; an **orientation** assigns a direction to each of its edges. A directed graph has the **tournament anti-Sidorenko property** (TAS) when its homomorphism density into every tournament satisfies the anti-Sidorenko inequality.

**TAS-tree conjecture.** For every undirected tree, there exists some orientation that has the tournament anti-Sidorenko property.

This conjecture was posed by Fox, Himwich, Zhou, and the second author. It is known for trees with exactly one vertex of even degree, but remains open in general.

full_parsed_record.statement:
An **undirected tree** is a connected graph with no cycles; an **orientation** assigns a direction to each of its edges. A directed graph has the **tournament anti-Sidorenko property** (TAS) when its homomorphism density into every tournament satisfies the anti-Sidorenko inequality.

**TAS-tree conjecture.** For every undirected tree, there exists some orientation that has the tournament anti-Sidorenko property.

This conjecture was posed by Fox, Himwich, Zhou, and the second author. It is known for trees with exactly one vertex of even degree, but remains open in general.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Xiaoyu He, Nitya Mani, Jiaxi Nie, Nathan Tung and Fan Wei, “New Sidorenko-type inequalities in tournaments”, arXiv:2512.11222 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11222

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “A small tree for which Conjecture remains open is the $2-3-4$ tree.”

372085.title: Maximum-size conjecture for 3-connected positroids excluding a uniform minor
372085.literal_statement:
Let $r$ and $\ell$ be integers with $r \ge 2$ and $\ell \ge 3$. A **3-connected rank-$r$ positroid** is a positroid of rank $r$ that is 3-connected, and a **$U_{2,\ell+2}$-minor-free** positroid has no minor isomorphic to the rank-two uniform matroid $U_{2,\ell+2}$.

**Maximum-size conjecture.** Every 3-connected rank-$r$ positroid with no $U_{2,\ell+2}$-minor has at most

$$
r + r\left\lfloor \frac{\ell - 1}{2} \right\rfloor
$$

elements if $\ell$ is odd, and at most

$$
r + r\left\lfloor \frac{\ell - 1}{2} \right\rfloor + 1
$$

elements if $\ell$ is even.

The conjectured bounds are attained by the families $W(r,\ell)$ for odd $\ell$ and $W(r,\ell)^+$ for even $\ell$, which the paper shows are 3-connected positroids with the required excluded-minor property. The conjecture asks whether these constructions maximize the number of elements among all such positroids; its status is not established in the supplied text.

362008.title: Tree-independence conjecture for biclique-free graphs of bounded induced matching treewidth
362008.literal_statement:
For a graph $G$, its induced matching treewidth is the minimum, over tree decompositions, of the maximum size of an induced matching whose edges intersect one bag; its tree-independence number is the minimum, over tree decompositions, of the maximum independence number of a bag. Let $K_{t,t}$ denote the complete bipartite graph with $t$ vertices in each part.

**Tree-independence conjecture.** For any two integers $k,t\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists an integer $r$ such that every graph with induced matching treewidth at most $k$ and no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{t,t}$ has tree-independence number at most $r$.

This would generalize known results relating induced matching treewidth, treewidth, and tree-independence number for classes excluding a fixed biclique. The conjecture remains open.
